newsitem.title: USA: Rural N.J teens held in pizza delivery men killings.
newsitem.headline: Rural N.J teens held in pizza delivery men killings.

text.p: - Two teenagers from this rural northwestern New Jersey town of 5,000 were ordered held in custody Monday, charged with the ambush-murders of two pizza delivery men Sunday night.

Thomas Koskovich, 18, and a 17-year-old juvenile were arrested Sunday night. Koskovich was ordered held in $1 million cash bail, and no bail was set for the juvenile, who was not identified because of his age.
They are charged with killing Georgio Gallara, 24-year-old owner of Tony's Pizza, and Jeremy Giordano, 22. Both were shot in their car, dragged to the ground and shot again.
Authorities said the accused youths called several pizza makers trying to get them to deliver to an abandoned house on a little-travelled road.

Police located the youths after tracing calls made to four other pizza shops back to a pay phone outside a local doughnut shop. Descriptions of the two youths by a shop employee enabled police to track down the two defendants, police said.
Sussex County Prosecutor Dennis O'Leary said the only motive he could suggest is that the accused were looking for a victim and found two.
